offense_class: Traffic Offense (not classified as crime under Title 2C)
elements: Operating a motor vehicle upon a highway or quasi-public area
While under the influence of intoxicating liquor OR with BAC of 0.08% or higher
OR with BAC of 0.10% or higher (enhanced penalties)
mandatory_minimum: 12-48 hours in Intoxicated Driver Resource Center (IDRC); license suspension 3 months (0.08-0.10) or 7-12 months (0.10+)
enhancements: BAC 0.10%+: higher fine tier ($500-$1,000)
Prior DWI within 10 years: second offense penalties
Refusal to take breath test: N.J.S.A. 39:4-50.4a — concurrent suspension
School zone DWI: double minimum penalties — N.J.S.A. 39:4-50(g)
notes: NJ uses 'Driving While Intoxicated' (DWI). Not a Title 2C crime — handled in Municipal Court. No jail for first offense except in aggravated cases. License suspension mandatory. Surcharge: $1,000/year for 3 years (MCCA).

elements: Operating a motor vehicle while under the influence
Prior DWI conviction within 10 years
mandatory_minimum: 48 hours jail; 30 days community service; 2-year license revocation
enhancements: Third offense: increased mandatory jail
School zone: double penalties
Refusal concurrent: additional suspension
notes: 30 days community service (in lieu of or in addition to jail). Ignition interlock device required during and after suspension. Surcharges apply for 3 years post-conviction.

statute_title: Driving While Intoxicated — Third or Subsequent Offense
elements: Operating a motor vehicle while under the influence
Two or more prior DWI convictions
mandatory_minimum: 180 days incarceration (90 days credit for inpatient rehab); 10-year license revocation
enhancements: Prior indictable conviction for DWI: enhanced
School zone: mandatory period doubled
notes: 10-year mandatory license revocation. Ignition interlock required. 90 days may be served in residential treatment program. Fourth offense also results in 10-year revocation with same jail time.

statute_title: Driving Under the Influence of Drugs
elements: Operating a motor vehicle
While under the influence of any narcotic, hallucinogenic, or habit-producing drug
Or with a Schedule I controlled dangerous substance (CDS) in urine
mandatory_minimum: Same as alcohol DWI; IDRC attendance required
enhancements: Drug DWI in school zone: double penalties
Prior DWI (alcohol or drug): same escalation applies
notes: NJ drug DWI uses same statute as alcohol DWI. Drug recognition expert (DRE) testimony used. Urine test for CDS presence. No per se level for most drugs except marijuana (still disputed).

elements: Causing the death of another person
By driving a vehicle recklessly
Including DWI as presumptive recklessness
mandatory_minimum: DWI-related: mandatory 3-5 year NERA period; 180-day license suspension
enhancements: DWI at time of death: no probation — N.J.S.A. 2C:11-5(b)(1)
Prior DWI conviction: 1st Degree treatment — N.J.S.A. 2C:11-5(c)(2)
NERA applies: 85% of sentence without parole
notes: DWI-related vehicular homicide presumptively reckless. No probation if DWI involved. Prior DWI conviction elevates to 1st Degree Crime (10-20 years). NERA applies to DWI vehicular homicide.

statute_title: Assault by Auto — DWI Causing Serious Bodily Injury
elements: Driving a vehicle recklessly or while intoxicated
Causing serious bodily injury to another person
mandatory_minimum: If DWI: no probation; mandatory Graves Act consideration if weapon used
enhancements: Prior DWI: upgraded from 3rd to 2nd Degree
Bodily injury only (not serious): 3rd Degree
School zone: 4th Degree standalone or enhanced on primary
notes: Assault by Auto is the NJ mechanism for DWI-injury cases. Seriousness of injury determines degree. Simple bodily injury is 4th Degree. Serious bodily injury is 3rd or 2nd Degree depending on DWI involvement.

elements: Operating a vehicle heedlessly
In willful or wanton disregard of the rights or safety of others
In a manner likely to endanger a person or property
enhancements: Second offense within 5 years: $500 fine, up to 3 months jail
Causing injury: assault by auto — N.J.S.A. 2C:12-1(c)
School zone: additional penalties
notes: Reckless driving is a motor vehicle offense handled in municipal court. Points assessed (5 points). First offense up to 60 days jail and $200 fine. Distinguished from careless driving (N.J.S.A. 39:4-97).

elements: Operating a motor vehicle upon a public highway
While driving privileges are suspended or revoked
enhancements: DWI suspension: 10-90 days mandatory jail — N.J.S.A. 39:3-40(f)
Third offense on DWI suspension: 180 days mandatory
Accident while driving suspended: additional civil liability
notes: DWI-related suspension driving carries mandatory jail time escalating with offense number. Non-DWI suspension driving is fine/community service. Insurance surcharges apply.

offense_class: Disorderly Persons Offense (small amounts for those under 21 or excess amounts)
elements: Knowing possession of marijuana
In excess of 6 ounces (adults 21+) or any amount (under 21)
Without lawful purpose
enhancements: Over 6 oz but under 1 pound: Disorderly Persons
1-5 pounds: 4th Degree Crime — N.J.S.A. 2C:35-5
Distribution: separate enhanced charges
notes: Adult recreational marijuana legalized in NJ effective April 2022 (up to 6 oz). Under-21 possession of any amount is civil violation or disorderly persons. Large quantities still criminal under distribution or trafficking statutes.

statute_title: Possession of CDS — Schedule I/II (Not Marijuana)
offense_class: 3rd Degree Crime (heroin, cocaine, meth, fentanyl); 4th Degree (Schedule III-IV)
elements: Knowingly and unlawfully possessing
A controlled dangerous substance (CDS)
Not pursuant to a valid prescription
enhancements: School zone: mandatory 1-year addition — N.J.S.A. 2C:35-7
Public housing: mandatory 1-year addition
Drug-free park: mandatory addition
Prior CDS conviction: parole ineligibility period may apply
notes: NJ's Drug Free Zone law doubles mandatory minimums for possession within 500 feet of school or within 500 feet of public housing. School zone carries mandatory 1-year parole ineligibility. Drug courts widely available.

elements: Knowingly or purposely manufacturing, distributing, dispensing, or possessing with intent
A controlled dangerous substance (CDS)
Without lawful authority
mandatory_minimum: 1st Degree (5+ oz heroin/cocaine or 25+ lbs marijuana): NERA — must serve 1/3 to 1/2 before parole; School zone: additional mandatory 1-3 years
enhancements: Within 500 feet of school: mandatory 1-3 year consecutive — N.J.S.A. 2C:35-7
Public housing zone: mandatory addition — N.J.S.A. 2C:35-7.1
1st Degree: NERA applies (85% of sentence)
Distributing to minor: upgrade one degree — N.J.S.A. 2C:35-6
Using juvenile to distribute: 3rd Degree standalone — N.J.S.A. 2C:35-6
notes: NJ's primary drug distribution statute. Quantity-based degrees: 5+ oz heroin/cocaine = 1st Degree; 1/2-5 oz = 2nd Degree; smaller = 3rd Degree. School zone add-on is commonly used prosecutorial tool.

elements: Conspiring with others as organizer, supervisor, or manager
Of a network of persons who engage in the production, manufacture, shipment, or distribution of CDS
Acting with respect to quantities in excess of statutory thresholds
enhancements: Drug kingpin conviction: no parole for 25 years
Forfeiture of all proceeds and assets
RICO charges concurrent
notes: New Jersey's drug kingpin statute. 25-year mandatory without parole. Designed for leaders of drug networks. Requires proof of supervisory role and quantity thresholds. Not merged with simple distribution.

statute_title: Use or Possession with Intent to Use Drug Paraphernalia
elements: Possession or use of drug paraphernalia
With intent to use in connection with a controlled dangerous substance violation
enhancements: Distribution of paraphernalia to minor: 4th Degree Crime — N.J.S.A. 2C:36-3
Prior CDS conviction: sentencing enhancement
notes: Paraphernalia charges frequently accompany CDS possession charges. Distribution of paraphernalia to person under 18 is a 4th Degree Crime.

elements: Purposely or knowingly causing the death of another person
OR purposely or knowingly causing serious bodily injury resulting in death
mandatory_minimum: 30-year parole disqualifier mandatory; life possible with 30-year minimum
enhancements: Murder of law enforcement: mandatory life, 30-year disqualifier
Murder by hired killer: mandatory life, 30-year disqualifier
Victim under 14 — murder by parent/guardian: 30-year disqualifier
Serial murder: death penalty replaced by life without parole
notes: NJ abolished death penalty in 2007. Maximum is Life LWOP or life with 30-year parole disqualifier. Murder is not classified as 1st or 2nd Degree in NJ Title 2C — it is 'murder' with sentencing structure. NERA does not apply — murder has its own parole disqualifier provisions.

elements: As principal or accomplice
During commission or attempted commission of robbery, sexual assault, arson, burglary, kidnapping, or carjacking
Causing the death of any person including co-felon
enhancements: Prior murder conviction: mandatory life
Multiple victims: multiple murder counts
notes: NJ felony murder is still 1st Degree Crime level (murder) — does not reduce to manslaughter. NJ Supreme Court has narrowed felony murder in recent years (State v. Doolin). Accomplice liability broadly applied.

elements: Recklessly causing the death of another person
Under circumstances manifesting extreme indifference to human life
mandatory_minimum: NERA applies: 85% of sentence before parole eligibility
enhancements: Victim is law enforcement: enhanced sentencing
DWI-related: no probation
Prior violent record: extended term
notes: NJ's aggravated manslaughter is a 1st Degree Crime — unusual among states. NERA applies. Regular manslaughter (N.J.S.A. 2C:11-4(b)) is 2nd Degree. Passion/provocation manslaughter is also 2nd Degree.

elements: Causing the death of another person
By driving a vehicle recklessly
On a public highway or quasi-public area
mandatory_minimum: If DWI involved: no probation; NERA may apply
enhancements: DWI at time: no probation, 180-day license suspension — N.J.S.A. 2C:11-5(b)
Prior DWI conviction: 1st Degree Crime — N.J.S.A. 2C:11-5(c)
Fleeing scene: enhanced sentencing
notes: NJ vehicular homicide under reckless driving is 2nd Degree. DWI-related vehicular homicide carries no probation and possible 1st Degree upgrade with prior DWI.

elements: Attempts to cause or purposely, knowingly, or recklessly causes bodily injury to another
OR negligently causes bodily injury with a deadly weapon
OR attempts by physical menace to put another in fear of imminent serious bodily injury
enhancements: Mutual fighting: Petty Disorderly Persons (30 days)
Against law enforcement/school employee: upgrade to 3rd Degree
Domestic setting: mandatory no-drop policy
notes: Simple assault in NJ is a disorderly persons offense (lower than crime). Mutual fighting reduces to Petty Disorderly Persons. Against certain protected victims (LEO, teacher, etc.) elevates to 3rd Degree Crime.

elements: Attempting to cause or causing serious bodily injury to another
OR causing bodily injury with a deadly weapon
OR causing significant bodily injury purposely or knowingly
OR pointing a firearm at another
enhancements: Serious bodily injury: 2nd Degree with NERA
Firearm: 2nd Degree and Graves Act may apply
Against law enforcement: 2nd Degree
Against elderly/disabled: 2nd Degree
notes: NJ's aggravated assault has multiple subsets. Pointing a firearm: 4th Degree. Using firearm to cause injury: 3rd Degree. Causing serious bodily injury: 2nd Degree with NERA. Strangulation: 3rd Degree — N.J.S.A. 2C:12-1(b)(12).

elements: Attempts to cause or purposely or knowingly causes
Bodily injury to another with a deadly weapon
mandatory_minimum: NERA may apply if weapon is firearm and serious bodily injury resulted
enhancements: Serious bodily injury caused: 2nd Degree with NERA
Firearm: Graves Act may trigger mandatory minimum
Against protected victim (teacher, elderly): enhanced degree
notes: 3rd Degree aggravated assault with deadly weapon. Upgraded to 2nd Degree if serious bodily injury results. Graves Act applies if firearm is used.

elements: In the course of committing a theft
Inflicting bodily injury or using force upon another
OR threatening another with immediate bodily injury
OR purposely putting another in fear
mandatory_minimum: NERA applies to both 1st and 2nd Degree robbery (85% of sentence)
enhancements: Armed with deadly weapon: 1st Degree Crime
Serious bodily injury inflicted: 1st Degree Crime
Victim is 60+: presumption of 1st Degree
Graves Act: firearm triggers mandatory minimum
notes: NERA (No Early Release Act) applies to robbery — must serve 85% of sentence. Armed robbery is 1st Degree (10-20 years with NERA). Unarmed robbery with no injury is 2nd Degree. Carjacking is separate offense under N.J.S.A. 2C:15-2.

elements: Robbery
While armed with a deadly weapon
OR while inflicting serious bodily injury
OR against a victim 60 years or older
mandatory_minimum: NERA: 85% of sentence (no parole until 85%); Graves Act mandatory minimum if firearm
enhancements: Graves Act firearm: mandatory 5-year minimum without parole — N.J.S.A. 2C:43-6(c)
Prior robbery conviction: Persistent Dangerous Offender designation possible
Multiple victims: consecutive sentences
notes: 1st Degree robbery carries NERA (85% served). Graves Act adds mandatory 5-year minimum if firearm is involved. Consecutive sentencing for multiple victims common. Graves Act waiver available through plea negotiation.

penalty_max: Life (if victim under 16 and not released unharmed)
elements: Knowingly unlawfully removing another from the place where found
OR unlawfully confining another for a substantial period
With purpose to hold for ransom, use as hostage, inflict bodily injury, terrorize, or facilitate crime
mandatory_minimum: NERA: 85% of sentence; 15-year parole ineligibility for crime against minor
enhancements: Victim under 16 not released: life with 25-year parole disqualifier
Victim is minor and sexually assaulted: enhanced — NERA minimum 25 years
Megan's Law registration if sex offense involved
notes: Kidnapping of a minor who is not released unharmed carries Life. NERA applies — must serve 85%. If victim is released in same or better condition, ordinary 1st Degree penalties apply. Parental kidnapping is a separate offense (N.J.S.A. 2C:13-4).

elements: Unlawfully taking a motor vehicle from another person
While using force or threatening force
OR while the person is in or immediately entering the vehicle
mandatory_minimum: NERA applies: 85% of sentence before parole; Graves Act if armed
enhancements: Firearm used: Graves Act — 5-year mandatory
Serious injury: enhanced sentence within 1st Degree
Multiple victims in vehicle: additional charges
notes: Carjacking is 1st Degree with NERA (85% must be served). Distinct from robbery. Maximum is Life. Graves Act applies if firearm present. Consecutive to other charges typical.

elements: Enters a structure
Without license or privilege to do so
With purpose to commit an offense therein
mandatory_minimum: NERA may apply if 2nd Degree (occupied structure burglary)
enhancements: Structure occupied at time: 2nd Degree
Armed with deadly weapon: 2nd Degree
Bodily injury caused: 2nd Degree with NERA
Prior burglary: extended term
notes: NJ burglary is 3rd Degree by default, 2nd Degree if structure is occupied or defendant is armed. NERA applies to 2nd Degree burglary. 'Structure' broadly defined to include vehicles, watercraft.

elements: Burglary of a structure
At a time when the structure is occupied
OR while armed with a deadly weapon
mandatory_minimum: NERA applies: 85% of sentence before parole
enhancements: Assault committed during burglary: aggravated assault concurrent
Firearm: Graves Act mandatory minimum
Multiple victims: enhanced sentencing
notes: NJ uses 2nd Degree burglary for occupied structures — equivalent to home invasion. NERA mandatory. Graves Act firearm minimum of 5 years without parole if gun is involved.

statute_title: Theft by Unlawful Taking or Disposition
elements: Purposely taking or exercising unlawful control
Over movable property of another
With purpose to deprive the owner of the property
enhancements: $75,000+: 2nd Degree
Under $500: Disorderly Persons
From person of elderly: upgraded one degree
notes: NJ consolidates theft offenses under N.J.S.A. 2C:20-1 et seq. All theft forms (robbery excepted) share the same grading by value. Theft of firearm: 4th Degree regardless of value.

elements: Purposely taking or exercising unlawful control
Over a motor vehicle
With purpose to deprive the owner
enhancements: Use of force or threat: carjacking — N.J.S.A. 2C:15-2
Chop shop operation: 2nd Degree — N.J.S.A. 2C:20-16
Prior auto theft: extended term
notes: Auto theft graded by value of vehicle. Most vehicles qualify as 3rd Degree. Carjacking is separate and more severe. Chop shops (N.J.S.A. 2C:20-16) carry 2nd Degree exposure.

elements: Purposely taking merchandise from a retail establishment
Without paying the full retail value
OR concealing merchandise, under-ringing, or destroying a theft detection device
enhancements: Organized retail theft ring: felony enhancement — N.J.S.A. 2C:20-11.3
Third offense: mandatory 90 days community service
Booster bag or device: separate charge — N.J.S.A. 2C:20-11(b)(6)
notes: NJ shoplifting: under $200 = Disorderly Persons; $200-$500 = 4th Degree; $500-$75,000 = 3rd Degree; $75,000+ = 2nd Degree. Organized retail theft is enhanced. Third offense adds mandatory community service.

elements: Starting a fire or causing an explosion
That places another person in danger of death or bodily injury
OR with purpose of destroying a building or occupied structure
enhancements: Person present in structure: 2nd Degree — NERA
Firefighter or investigator injured: enhanced sentencing
Insurance fraud arson: concurrent fraud charges
notes: NJ arson distinguishes reckless burning (3rd Degree) from purposeful with persons endangered (2nd Degree with NERA). Aggravated arson provisions for occupied structures. Insurance fraud arson commonly prosecuted together.

offense_class: 2nd-4th Degree Crime or Disorderly Persons (damage value-based)
elements: Purposely or knowingly damaging tangible property of another
OR recklessly or negligently damaging property with fire, explosives, or other dangerous means
enhancements: $75,000+: 2nd Degree
Under $500: Disorderly Persons
Bias/hate crime motivation: bias intimidation statute adds additional charge — N.J.S.A. 2C:16-1
notes: NJ Criminal Mischief graded by value of damage. Graffiti under N.J.S.A. 2C:17-3(b). Bias-motivated vandalism triggers separate N.J.S.A. 2C:16-1 bias intimidation charge.

offense_class: Underlying offense classification applies (Disorderly Persons to 1st Degree)
elements: Commission of a predicate offense listed in N.J.S.A. 2C:25-19
Against a protected person (current or former spouse, domestic partner, household member, parent of common child)
Predicate offenses include: assault, stalking, terroristic threats, criminal mischief, trespass, burglary, harassment, sexual assault, homicide, kidnapping, bias crime
mandatory_minimum: TRO/FRO issued upon arrest; no-bail warrant may issue
enhancements: Strangulation: 3rd Degree aggravated assault — N.J.S.A. 2C:12-1(b)(12)
FRO violation: 4th Degree Crime — N.J.S.A. 2C:29-9
Prior DV conviction: enhanced sentencing on predicate offense
notes: NJ's Prevention of Domestic Violence Act (PDVA) creates civil protection order framework. Criminal prosecution uses underlying predicate offense. Strangulation is specifically elevated to 3rd Degree aggravated assault.

offense_class: 4th Degree Crime (first); 3rd Degree (repeat or with restraining order)
elements: Purposefully or knowingly engaging in a course of conduct
Directed at a specific person
That would cause a reasonable person to fear for safety or suffer emotional distress
enhancements: While under a restraining order: 3rd Degree
Second or subsequent conviction: 3rd Degree
Using social media or electronic communications: same statute applies — cyberstalking
notes: NJ stalking statute covers both physical and electronic (cyber) stalking. 'Course of conduct' requires 2+ acts. Second offense or violation of TRO/FRO elevates to 3rd Degree.

elements: Existence of a valid Final Restraining Order
Defendant had knowledge of the order
Defendant purposely or knowingly violated a term of the order
enhancements: Assault committed during violation: concurrent aggravated assault
Stalking during violation: concurrent stalking charge
Multiple violations: multiple counts
notes: Violation of NJ FRO is a 4th Degree Crime. TRO violation is a contempt matter handled civilly. Criminal violation requires a Final Restraining Order, not just TRO. Also triggers contempt proceedings.

statute_title: Child Abuse — Cruelty and Neglect of Children
offense_class: 4th Degree Crime (neglect); 3rd Degree Crime (abuse with injury); 2nd Degree (serious injury)
elements: Parent or person responsible for the care of a child
Inflicting physical or mental harm upon the child
OR allowing the child to be subjected to abuse
enhancements: Sexual abuse element: CSC statute concurrent
Child death: murder or aggravated manslaughter
Pattern of abuse: extended term
notes: NJ child abuse statute under Title 9. Aggravated criminal assault of a child under N.J.S.A. 2C:12-1 also applies. Mandatory reporting law (N.J.S.A. 9:6-8.10) applies broadly. DCPP involvement concurrent.

elements: Parent or guardian
Abandoning, refusing to provide, or failing to provide
Necessary care (food, clothing, shelter, medical care) for a child
enhancements: Serious harm results: upgraded to 3rd or 2nd Degree under N.J.S.A. 2C:24-4(a)
Death resulting: murder or manslaughter charges
Prior neglect adjudication: sentencing enhancement
notes: NJ child endangerment under N.J.S.A. 2C:24-4(a) is the companion criminal statute. DCPP/DYFS proceedings run concurrently. Endangering welfare of children (N.J.S.A. 2C:24-4) is the more commonly used criminal charge.

statute_title: Certain Persons Not to Have Weapons
elements: Having been convicted of specific crimes or offenses
Possessing, owning, purchasing, or controlling a firearm
OR having been convicted of domestic violence predicate and possessing any weapon
mandatory_minimum: Graves Act: 5-year mandatory minimum without parole — N.J.S.A. 2C:43-6(c)
enhancements: Graves Act mandatory applies to ALL prohibited persons firearm cases
Use in crime: additional concurrent charges
Prior Certain Persons conviction: extended term mandatory
notes: NJ's felon-in-possession equivalent. 2nd Degree Crime. Graves Act applies — mandatory 5-year minimum without parole. Also applies to persons convicted of DV predicate offenses who possess ANY weapon, not just firearms. One of the most heavily prosecuted NJ gun laws.

elements: Carrying, possessing, or controlling a handgun
Without first having obtained a Permit to Carry a Handgun
Outside of the person's dwelling place or place of business
mandatory_minimum: Graves Act: 5-year mandatory minimum without parole
enhancements: Firearm is loaded: sentencing enhancement
In school zone: mandatory additional 3-5 years
Graves Act waiver available through plea to 2nd Degree without mandatory minimum
notes: NJ had most restrictive carry laws in US before Bruen (2022). Post-Bruen, shall-issue permits available but NJ still maintains Graves Act mandatory minimum for permit-less carry. 2nd Degree with mandatory 5-year minimum under Graves Act.

statute_title: Graves Act — Mandatory Minimum for Firearm Offenses
offense_class: Mandatory minimum sentence enhancement (not standalone offense)
elements: Conviction for a Graves Act offense (firearm-related crime under N.J.S.A. 2C:39-1 et seq.)
With exception of certain non-violent possession offenses
Including unlawful possession, possession by certain persons, using firearm in commission of crime
mandatory_minimum: 1/2 of sentence or 5 years, whichever is greater, without parole eligibility
enhancements: Prior Graves Act offense: mandatory term increases
Second Graves Act offense: 10-year mandatory without parole
Graves Act waiver: Prosecutor may downgrade — requires court approval
notes: The Graves Act is NJ's signature gun law — applies to all N.J.S.A. 2C:39-series convictions. The mandatory minimum is the GREATER of half the sentence OR 5 years. No parole during mandatory period. Waiver available but rarely granted in practice.

statute_title: Aggravated Assault with Firearm / Possession of Firearm for Unlawful Purpose
elements: Attempt to cause serious bodily injury using a firearm
OR possession of a firearm with purpose to use it unlawfully against another
mandatory_minimum: Graves Act: 5-year mandatory minimum; NERA: 85% of sentence
enhancements: Serious bodily injury inflicted: NERA in full force
Victim is law enforcement: enhanced sentencing
Prior violent felony: extended term
notes: Both aggravated assault with firearm and possession for unlawful purpose are 2nd Degree with Graves Act mandatory and NERA. Frequently charged together. Most common felony gun charges in NJ.

elements: Obtaining personal identifying information of another
Without authorization
With purpose to fraudulently obtain a benefit or to injure or defraud
enhancements: 5+ victims or $75,000+ loss: 2nd Degree
$500-$75,000 or 2-4 victims: 3rd Degree
Under $500 or 1 victim: 4th Degree
Victim is 62+: additional $10,000 fine
notes: NJ identity theft tiered by number of victims and financial loss. Senior victim (62+) triggers mandatory $10,000 fine. Restitution mandatory. Impersonation using internet or computer carries additional charges.

elements: Using a credit card with knowledge that it is stolen, revoked, or used without authorization
With intent to defraud
Obtaining money, goods, services, or anything of value
enhancements: Skimming device: additional charges — N.J.S.A. 2C:21-6.1
Identity theft component: concurrent charges
Multiple cards/victims: multiple counts
notes: NJ credit card fraud under N.J.S.A. 2C:21-6. Skimming devices are separately criminalized under N.J.S.A. 2C:21-6.1. Restitution mandatory.

elements: Knowingly making or causing to be made
A false, fictitious, fraudulent, or misleading statement
In connection with an insurance claim or application
enhancements: Personal injury fraud scheme (PIP fraud): mandatory criminal referral
Healthcare provider fraud: additional penalties — N.J.S.A. 2C:21-4.3
Organized fraud ring: 2nd Degree enhancement
notes: NJ Insurance Fraud Prevention Act. Auto insurance (PIP/personal injury) fraud is highly prevalent and prosecuted. Healthcare provider insurance fraud has enhanced penalties. Civil enforcement also available through OIC.

statute_title: Theft by Breach of Fiduciary Duty (Embezzlement)
elements: Being a fiduciary
Knowingly dealing with property entrusted to them
In a manner they know to be incompatible with their fiduciary duty
enhancements: Public officer or official: 2nd Degree regardless of amount — N.J.S.A. 2C:20-9(c)
Elderly victim: one degree enhanced
Organized scheme: additional conspiracy charges
notes: NJ consolidates embezzlement under theft by breach of fiduciary duty. Public officer theft is automatically 2nd Degree. Restitution mandatory.

elements: Committing an act of sexual penetration
Under aggravated circumstances: victim under 13; victim 13-15 and defendant authority figure; force, coercion, or incapacitation; victim physically helpless; armed with weapon
mandatory_minimum: NERA: 85% of sentence must be served before parole eligibility
enhancements: Victim under 13: NERA mandatory, life possible
Repeat offenders: Megan's Law Tier 3 registration (lifetime)
Prior sex offense conviction: extended term
Predatory Sex Offenders Act: additional civil commitment
notes: NJ uses 'aggravated sexual assault' (1st Degree) and 'sexual assault' (2nd Degree). NERA mandatory for 1st Degree — 85% served before parole. Megan's Law registration required. Parole Supervision for Life (PSL) mandatory for adults.

elements: Sexual penetration with another person
Using physical force or coercion
OR victim is 16 or 17 and defendant has supervisory or disciplinary authority
OR victim is 13-15 and defendant is at least 4 years older
mandatory_minimum: NERA: 85% of sentence; Parole Supervision for Life (PSL) mandatory
enhancements: Prior sex offense: extended term
Megan's Law Tier 2 or 3 registration
Position of trust: sentencing enhancement
Special Probation (BIRIA): available in limited circumstances
notes: 2nd Degree sexual assault (penetration with force or statutory age circumstances). NERA mandatory. PSL (lifetime parole supervision) required for all adults convicted of sexual assault. Megan's Law registration mandatory.

statute_title: Aggravated Criminal Sexual Contact — Third Degree
elements: Sexual contact (not penetration)
Under aggravated circumstances (same as aggravated sexual assault but contact only)
Including force, incapacity, victim age under 13
mandatory_minimum: NERA may apply depending on circumstances
enhancements: Prior sex offense: extended term
Megan's Law registration required
PSL mandatory for adults
notes: 3rd Degree for sexual contact under aggravated circumstances. Criminal sexual contact (4th Degree, N.J.S.A. 2C:14-3(b)) covers non-aggravated sexual contact with force.

elements: Sexual contact
Using physical force or coercion
Without specific aggravating circumstances of 3rd Degree
enhancements: Prior sex offense: enhanced to 3rd Degree
Megan's Law registration required
PSL mandatory
notes: Lowest-level NJ sex offense. 4th Degree Criminal Sexual Contact. Megan's Law and PSL still apply despite misdemeanor-equivalent severity. Force or coercion required — not just offensive touching.

offense_class: Disorderly Persons Offense; 4th Degree if victim under 13
elements: Exposing intimate parts
For the purpose of arousing or gratifying sexual desire
Under circumstances likely to cause affront or alarm
enhancements: Victim under 13: 4th Degree Crime
Online exposure/transmission: computer crime charges added
School zone: municipal ordinance may apply
notes: NJ uses 'Lewdness' rather than indecent exposure. Disorderly Persons for general lewdness, 4th Degree if victim is under 13. Megan's Law registration possible for 4th Degree lewd acts against minors.

penalty_max: 6 months (Disorderly Persons); 18 months (4th Degree); 5 years (3rd Degree)
elements: Soliciting or promoting prostitution
Engaging in sexual activity as a business for compensation
OR profiting from prostitution of another
enhancements: Promoting prostitution of minor under 18: 3rd Degree
Compelling prostitution through force: 1st Degree — N.J.S.A. 2C:13-8
Human trafficking: additional enhanced charges
notes: NJ prostitution law under N.J.S.A. 2C:34-1. Solicitation is Disorderly Persons. Promoting is 4th Degree. Promoting minor's prostitution is 3rd Degree. Sex trafficking of minors prosecuted under N.J.S.A. 2C:13-8.

elements: Recruiting, luring, enticing, or harboring a person
Through force, fraud, or coercion
For the purpose of commercial sexual activity
mandatory_minimum: NERA: 85% of sentence; victim under 18: no probation
enhancements: Victim under 18: mandatory life imprisonment or 20-year minimum
Multiple victims: consecutive sentences
Use of controlled substance to control victim: additional CDS charges
notes: NJ Human Trafficking statute under N.J.S.A. 2C:13-8. Minors cannot consent — no defense of consent for trafficking of persons under 18. Asset forfeiture. Victim services and safe harbor provisions under N.J.S.A. 2C:13-9.

elements: Appearing in a public place
Under the influence of alcohol or a controlled substance
Manifesting a purpose to cause public inconvenience, annoyance, or alarm
enhancements: Creating serious hazard: disorderly conduct upgrade
DWI if operating a vehicle: N.J.S.A. 39:4-50
notes: NJ does not have a standalone 'public intoxication' statute. Charged as Disorderly Conduct (Petty Disorderly Persons) or under municipal ordinances. DWI applies when operating a vehicle.

elements: Engaging in fighting, threatening, or violent behavior
OR creating a hazardous or physically offensive condition
OR using offensive, threatening, or abusive language in a public place
enhancements: Simple assault concurrent if physical contact
Mutual fighting: Petty Disorderly Persons (same)
Near school or public event: local ordinance may enhance
notes: NJ disorderly conduct is Petty Disorderly Persons (30 days max). Distinguished from simple assault (Disorderly Persons, 6 months) when no physical contact occurs. Commonly used for altercations.

offense_class: 4th Degree Crime (dwelling); Disorderly Persons (other structure); Petty Disorderly (land)
elements: Entering or surreptitiously remaining in any structure
Knowing that permission has been denied
Without license, privilege, or lawful reason
enhancements: Dwelling: 4th Degree Crime
School building: 4th Degree
Other structure: Disorderly Persons
Open land: Petty Disorderly Persons
notes: NJ trespass escalates based on type of structure. Dwelling trespass is 4th Degree Crime. Other structures are Disorderly Persons. Open land is Petty Disorderly. Defiant trespasser (refuses to leave) included.

offense_class: Disorderly Persons Offense (no force); 3rd Degree (flight/force used)
penalty_max: 6 months (no force); 5 years (flight or force — 3rd Degree)
elements: Knowingly preventing or attempting to prevent a law enforcement officer
From effecting a lawful arrest
By creating a substantial risk of bodily injury or employing means requiring substantial force
enhancements: Flight: 3rd Degree
Officer injured: aggravated assault concurrent
Use of vehicle to flee: eluding — N.J.S.A. 2C:29-2(b)
notes: NJ resisting arrest: passive resistance is Disorderly Persons; active resistance with flight or force is 3rd Degree Crime. Eluding police in vehicle is separately 2nd or 3rd Degree under N.J.S.A. 2C:29-2(b).

statute_title: Obstructing Administration of Law or Other Governmental Function
offense_class: Disorderly Persons Offense; 4th Degree if force or flight
elements: Purposely obstructing, impairing, or perverting the administration of law
Or other governmental function
Using force, violence, physical interference, or obstacle, or an independently unlawful act
enhancements: Force used: 4th Degree
Official misconduct (official doing it): 2nd Degree — N.J.S.A. 2C:30-2
Witness tampering concurrent: N.J.S.A. 2C:28-5
notes: NJ obstruction is broadly worded. Passive obstruction is Disorderly Persons; use of force elevates to 4th Degree. Tampering with witness/evidence are separate offenses.

elements: In any official proceeding
Making a false statement under oath or affirmation
With knowledge of its falsity
With purpose to mislead a public servant in performing his official function
enhancements: False swearing (not in official proceeding): 4th Degree — N.J.S.A. 2C:28-2
False statements to police: hindering apprehension — N.J.S.A. 2C:29-3
Perjury in capital case: aggravating factor
notes: NJ perjury is 3rd Degree Crime. 'Official proceeding' includes trials, hearings, depositions, and administrative proceedings. Subornation of perjury is 3rd Degree under N.J.S.A. 2C:28-3.

statute_title: Bribery in Official and Political Matters
elements: Offering, conferring, agreeing to confer, or soliciting, accepting, or agreeing to accept
A benefit as consideration for a vote, opinion, recommendation, decision, or exercise of discretion
By a public servant, party official, or voter
enhancements: Commercial bribery: 2nd Degree if value exceeds $200 — N.J.S.A. 2C:21-10
Receiving unlawful benefit (public servant): 2nd Degree — N.J.S.A. 2C:27-9
Official misconduct: additional 2nd Degree charge — N.J.S.A. 2C:30-2
notes: NJ bribery covers political and official corruption. 3rd Degree for giving or receiving. Official misconduct (N.J.S.A. 2C:30-2) is a 2nd Degree parallel charge for officials acting corruptly.

statute_title: Financial Facilitation of Criminal Activity (Money Laundering)
elements: Knowingly engaging in a financial transaction
With proceeds derived from criminal activity
With intent to conceal or disguise the nature, location, source, ownership, or control of the proceeds
mandatory_minimum: None; NERA may apply for 1st Degree
enhancements: $500,000+: 1st Degree
Under $75,000: 3rd Degree
Drug trafficking underlying: federal concurrent prosecution
Forfeiture of all proceeds
notes: NJ money laundering under N.J.S.A. 2C:21-25. Asset forfeiture available. Federal charges under 18 U.S.C. § 1956 frequently concurrent for organized schemes.

elements: Conducting or participating in an enterprise
Through a pattern of racketeering activity
With knowledge or intent to benefit the enterprise
mandatory_minimum: NERA may apply depending on predicate acts
enhancements: Drug trafficking predicate: enhanced penalties
Murder predicate: 1st Degree enhancement
Financial benefit forfeiture
Federal RICO concurrent: 18 U.S.C. § 1962
notes: NJ RICO under N.J.S.A. 2C:41-1 et seq. (New Jersey Criminal Justice Act). Requires 'pattern' of at least 2 acts within 10 years. Civil RICO available to private plaintiffs. Asset forfeiture.

elements: Obtaining property of another by threatening
To inflict bodily injury, commit a crime, accuse of a crime, expose secrets, or abuse official position
enhancements: Threat of bodily harm: concurrent assault charges
Use of mail or wire: federal extortion — 18 U.S.C. § 875
Organized crime context: NJ RICO charges
notes: NJ extortion classified under theft statutes (N.J.S.A. 2C:20-5). Graded as 2nd Degree when threat involved — unlike other theft forms graded by value. Federal Hobbs Act extortion (18 U.S.C. § 1951) frequently used for organized crime.

offense_class: Same grading as theft by value (2nd-4th Degree or Disorderly Persons)
elements: Purposely receiving, retaining, or disposing of movable property of another
Knowing it has been stolen
OR believing it is probably stolen
With purpose to benefit from it or to prevent the owner from recovering it
enhancements: Motor vehicle: enhanced if chop shop operation
Jewelry, firearms: value-based grading applies
Commercial fencing: multiple counts or racketeering
notes: NJ receiving stolen property graded same as theft by value. Knowledge of stolen status may be inferred from circumstances. Professional fencing operations subject to racketeering charges.

elements: Altering, completing, executing, or authenticating
Any writing or object
With purpose to defraud or injure another
enhancements: Government documents, currency: 3rd Degree
Prescription forgery: 3rd Degree with CDS concurrent
Fraudulent use of forged document: additional uttering charge — N.J.S.A. 2C:21-2
notes: NJ forgery under N.J.S.A. 2C:21-1. Uttering forged document is separate offense under N.J.S.A. 2C:21-2. Counterfeit currency is federal offense. Check kiting has separate provisions.

offense_class: Same as the most serious offense in the conspiracy (one degree below for non-1st Degree)
penalty_max: Varies (Life if murder conspiracy; otherwise one degree below substantive offense)
elements: Agreeing with one or more persons to commit an offense
With purpose of promoting or facilitating its commission
AND an overt act in furtherance
enhancements: Conspiracy to commit 1st Degree crime: 1st Degree conspiracy
Drug distribution conspiracy: school zone mandatory minimums may apply
Continuing conspiracy: Wharton's Rule considerations
notes: NJ conspiracy graded one degree below the target offense, except conspiracy to commit 1st Degree crime remains 1st Degree. Overt act required. Withdrawal defense available with proper notice.

offense_class: One degree below the completed offense
penalty_max: One degree below completed offense (attempt to commit 1st Degree = 2nd Degree)
elements: Purposely engaging in conduct which would constitute the crime if the attendant circumstances were as a reasonable person would believe them to be
OR doing something which is a substantial step in a course of conduct planned to culminate in the crime
enhancements: Attempt to commit murder: 1st Degree Crime
Attempt at 1st Degree: treated as 1st Degree for sentencing purposes under N.J.S.A. 2C:5-4
Substantial step must be more than mere preparation
notes: NJ attempt graded one degree below completed offense. Attempt of 1st Degree is still 1st Degree. Abandonment is an affirmative defense if voluntary and complete. 'Substantial step' test used.

elements: With the purpose of promoting or facilitating the commission of the offense
Soliciting another person to commit it
OR aiding, agreeing to aid, or attempting to aid another person in planning or committing it
mandatory_minimum: Same as principal (Graves Act/NERA apply equally)
enhancements: Active participation increases culpability
Getaway driver subject to same charges as principal
Accessory after the fact: hindering apprehension — N.J.S.A. 2C:29-3
notes: NJ accomplice liability — same punishment as principal. Accessory after the fact is not an accomplice in NJ — charged under hindering apprehension (N.J.S.A. 2C:29-3). Graves Act and NERA apply equally to accomplices.

statute_title: Leaving the Scene of an Accident (Personal Injury)
elements: Operating a motor vehicle involved in an accident resulting in injury to a person
Knowingly failing to stop
Or to provide name, address, and vehicle identification
enhancements: Death resulting: 2nd Degree — N.J.S.A. 2C:12-1.1
DWI concurrent: enhanced sentencing
Second offense: extended term
notes: NJ elevated leaving the scene of injury/death to 3rd/2nd Degree indictable offense. Property damage only: Title 39 motor vehicle offense. License suspension mandatory. Restitution to victim required.

statute_title: Abuse, Neglect, Exploitation of Vulnerable Adults
elements: Person responsible for care of a vulnerable adult
Willfully abusing, neglecting, or mistreating
OR allowing abuse, neglect, or exploitation
enhancements: Financial exploitation concurrent: N.J.S.A. 2C:21-17.1
Death resulting: aggravated manslaughter
Prior conviction: extended term
notes: NJ Adult Protective Services Act — criminal provisions. Title 2C financial exploitation of vulnerable adult under N.J.S.A. 2C:21-17.1 runs concurrently. Mandatory reporting.

statute_title: Theft or Wrongful Taking — Elderly or Vulnerable Person
offense_class: 4th-2nd Degree Crime (value-based; one degree elevated from standard theft)
elements: Committing theft or unlawful taking
From a person who is 60 years of age or older
Or from a vulnerable adult (disabled/incapacitated)
enhancements: Amount over $75,000: 2nd Degree
$1,000-$75,000: 3rd Degree (standard theft 3rd would be $500-$75,000)
Financial institution employee: enhanced sentencing
Caregiver: breach of fiduciary enhancement
notes: NJ elevates theft crimes against elderly or vulnerable adults by one degree. $1,000 threshold for 3rd Degree (vs. $500 for standard theft). Restitution mandatory. Both civil and criminal remedies available.

offense_class: 3rd Degree Crime; 2nd Degree if threat to commit crime of 1st or 2nd Degree
elements: Threatening to commit any crime of violence
With purpose to terrorize another
OR threatening to commit a crime of violence in reckless disregard of the risk of causing terror
enhancements: Threat to commit 1st or 2nd Degree crime: 2nd Degree — N.J.S.A. 2C:12-3(b)
School threat: separate enhanced provisions — N.J.S.A. 2C:33-3
Online threat: same statute, computer charges may be added
notes: NJ terroristic threats is 3rd Degree (base) or 2nd Degree (if the threatened crime is 1st or 2nd Degree). Threatening school or community is 3rd Degree under N.J.S.A. 2C:33-3. Harassment (N.J.S.A. 2C:33-4) is a lower-level alternative.

statute_title: Possession of Other Weapons Without License
elements: Having in one's possession any weapon
Under circumstances not manifestly appropriate for such lawful uses as it may have
Without license or legal authority
enhancements: Handgun: N.J.S.A. 2C:39-5(b) — 2nd Degree with Graves Act
Prohibited weapon (switchblade, brass knuckles): additional charges — N.J.S.A. 2C:39-3
School zone: mandatory additional term — N.J.S.A. 2C:39-5(e)
notes: NJ regulates 'weapons' broadly. Specific prohibited weapons under N.J.S.A. 2C:39-3. Handgun possession without permit is 2nd Degree (Graves Act). School zone weapon possession carries mandatory additional sentence.

statute_title: Possession of Firearm in School Zone
elements: Possessing or carrying a weapon
In or within 1,000 feet of school property or school bus
Without authorization
mandatory_minimum: Graves Act applies for firearm: 5-year mandatory
enhancements: Firearm: 2nd Degree + Graves Act
Prior weapons conviction: extended term
During school hours: aggravating factor
notes: NJ Gun-Free School Zone Act makes possession of firearm on school grounds a 2nd Degree Crime with Graves Act. Distance extends to 1,000 feet of school property. Both state and federal (18 U.S.C. § 922(q)) apply.

offense_class: 4th Degree Crime (general false alarm); 3rd Degree (targeting school/mass transit)
elements: Initiating or circulating a report or warning
Knowing it is false or baseless
Which would prompt official emergency response or public evacuation
mandatory_minimum: None; restitution mandatory for response costs
enhancements: School or house of worship: 3rd Degree — N.J.S.A. 2C:33-3(e)
Emergency services mobilized: mandatory restitution
Multiple threats: multiple counts
notes: False public alarm (bomb threat) escalated to 3rd Degree for school and religious institution threats. Restitution for evacuation costs mandatory. Juvenile offenders frequently charged.

elements: Intentionally or knowingly
Overdriving, overloading, torturing, or killing an animal
OR causing unnecessary suffering to an animal
enhancements: Multiple animals: multiple counts
Animal fighting: 4th Degree — N.J.S.A. 4:22-24
Prior conviction: extended term
notes: NJ animal cruelty under N.J.S.A. 4:22-17 et seq. Upgraded from summary offense to 4th Degree Crime in 2016 (Jax's Law). Animal fighting is separately criminalized. SPCA has law enforcement authority.

offense_class: Revocation proceeding; penalty up to original term
penalty_max: Remaining term or maximum of original offense
elements: Defendant on a probation term
Willfully violating a condition of probation
Established by preponderance of evidence at violation hearing
enhancements: New criminal offense while on probation: consecutive sentencing likely
Technical violations: stepped responses (community service, jail)
PSL (Parole Supervision for Life) violations: NJSP Parole Board jurisdiction
notes: NJ probation violations heard before sentencing judge. No jury. Preponderance standard. Court may continue, modify, or revoke to impose custodial sentence up to original maximum. Drug court technical violations have their own graduated responses.

penalty_max: Return to prison for remainder of sentence
elements: Person on parole
Violating conditions of parole
Including new criminal conduct, technical violations, or absconding
enhancements: New crime while on parole: consecutive term likely
Absconding: warrant issued; no bail typical
notes: NJ State Parole Board jurisdiction. Due process rights under Morrissey v. Brewer apply. Parole Supervision for Life (PSL) violations for sex offenders handled by NJ State Parole Board with more supervision.

offense_class: 3rd Degree Crime (escape from institution); 4th Degree (leave temporary release)
elements: Escaping from official detention
OR using force, threat, or deception to escape
Without authorization
enhancements: Force or weapon used: additional assault charges
Injuring corrections officer: aggravated assault concurrent
Conspiracy to escape: additional charges
notes: NJ escape is 3rd Degree for facility escape. Failure to return from furlough is 4th Degree. Sentence for escape runs consecutive to existing sentence.

offense_class: 4th Degree Crime; 3rd Degree if bomb threat or mass casualty
elements: Knowingly giving or causing a false report to be given
To any law enforcement or civil authority
Reporting that an offense has been committed or a fire is burning
mandatory_minimum: None; restitution mandatory if emergency response triggered
enhancements: Bomb threat or terrorist act: 3rd Degree — N.J.S.A. 2C:33-3
Emergency response costs: mandatory restitution
Prior false report: sentencing enhancement
notes: NJ false report to law enforcement is 4th Degree. False bomb threat separately prosecuted as 3rd Degree under N.J.S.A. 2C:33-3. Restitution for response costs. Distinct from false statements in official proceedings (perjury).

elements: Purposely or knowingly and without authorization accessing
A computer system, network, or data
Altering, damaging, deleting, or obtaining data
enhancements: $75,000+ damage: 2nd Degree
Under $500: 4th Degree
Government systems: enhanced federal charges
Healthcare data breach: HIPAA federal parallel
notes: NJ Computer Criminal Activity Act under N.J.S.A. 2C:20-23 et seq. Graded by financial damage caused. Federal CFAA (18 U.S.C. § 1030) charges frequently concurrent for interstate computer crimes.

elements: Willfully failing to file a required tax return
OR willfully making or subscribing a false tax return
With intent to evade or defeat any tax
enhancements: Multiple years of non-filing: multiple counts
Sales tax fraud: N.J.S.A. 54:32B-13
Federal concurrent IRS prosecution
Offshore account concealment: additional charges
notes: NJ Division of Taxation handles state tax fraud. Federal IRS prosecution concurrent. Sales tax fraud separately prosecuted under N.J.S.A. 54:32B-13. Restitution and interest mandatory.

offense_class: 2nd-4th Degree Crime (state, loss-based); federal: up to 20 years
elements: A scheme or artifice to defraud
Using wire communications, internet, or electronic means
Obtaining money or property through false pretenses
enhancements: Financial institution victim: 30 years federal
COVID/disaster fraud: enhanced federal
Mail fraud concurrent: 18 U.S.C. § 1341
notes: Federal wire fraud frequently charged for interstate fraud. NJ state fraud under N.J.S.A. 2C:21-4 covers scheme to defraud. Both charges often filed together.

elements: Knowingly making false statements
In connection with a residential mortgage loan
With intent to defraud a lender, borrower, or government entity
enhancements: $75,000+ loss: 2nd Degree
Multiple loans: multiple counts
Bank fraud: federal prosecution concurrent — 18 U.S.C. § 1344
Real estate professional: licensing consequences
notes: NJ Residential Mortgage Fraud Act under N.J.S.A. 2C:21-4.5. Federal bank fraud charges frequently concurrent. Straw buyer schemes and appraisal fraud common patterns.

statute_title: Possession of Child Sexual Abuse Material (CSAM)
elements: Knowingly possessing
Any photograph, film, or other material depicting a child
In a sexually explicit manner
enhancements: Distribution or showing: 3rd Degree — N.J.S.A. 2C:24-4(b)(3)
Production: 2nd Degree — N.J.S.A. 2C:24-4(b)(2)
Federal concurrent prosecution: 18 U.S.C. § 2252
Prior sex conviction: extended term
notes: NJ CSAM possession is 4th Degree. Each image may be a separate count under N.J.S.A. 2C:24-4(b)(5) (each depicts a separate victim). Megan's Law registration mandatory. Federal charges typical for internet-based distribution.

statute_title: Production/Creation of Child Sexual Abuse Material
elements: Filming, photographing, or reproducing
A minor engaged in sexually explicit conduct
For the purpose of creating CSAM
mandatory_minimum: NERA: 85% of sentence; Megan's Law registration mandatory
enhancements: Child under 13: enhanced sentencing within 2nd Degree
Prior sex offense: extended term
Distribution of material: additional concurrent charges
notes: 2nd Degree CSAM production in NJ — NERA applies (85% served before parole). Federal prosecution under 18 U.S.C. § 2251 typically concurrent. PSL (Parole Supervision for Life) mandatory.

offense_class: Petty Disorderly Persons Offense; 4th Degree if pattern toward bias
elements: Making or causing to be made a communication in a manner likely to cause annoyance or alarm
OR striking, kicking, shoving, or subjecting to offensive touching
OR engaging in any other course of alarming conduct with purpose to alarm or annoy
enhancements: Bias-based harassment: 4th Degree — N.J.S.A. 2C:16-1 concurrent
Cyberstalking/electronic harassment: stalking charges may apply
Against DV protected person: predicate for FRO
notes: NJ harassment (Petty Disorderly) is a common predicate for domestic violence FRO proceedings. 4th Degree elevation for bias-based harassment. Electronic harassment increasingly charged.

offense_class: 3rd Degree Crime (default); 2nd Degree if creates risk of injury
elements: Operating a motor vehicle
After being signaled by a police officer to stop
Intentionally fleeing or attempting to elude the officer
mandatory_minimum: License revocation mandatory; NERA may apply for 2nd Degree
enhancements: Creates risk of death or injury to another: 2nd Degree — N.J.S.A. 2C:29-2(b)
High-speed chase injuring bystander: NERA applicable
OWI concurrent: enhanced sentencing
notes: NJ eluding is 3rd Degree by default, elevated to 2nd Degree with risk of injury (NERA). License revocation 6 months to 2 years. Consecutive to other charges arising from same incident.

offense_class: 3rd Degree Crime (standalone); elevated by underlying offense degree
elements: Committing a predicate offense
Because of, or in a manner reasonably calculated to put another person in fear on account of
Race, color, religion, gender, disability, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, or ethnicity
enhancements: If the underlying crime is 1st Degree: bias intimidation is 2nd Degree
If underlying is 2nd/3rd Degree: bias intimidation is 3rd Degree
If Disorderly Persons: bias intimidation is 4th Degree
Mandatory civil penalty to victim
notes: NJ bias intimidation statute. Conviction elevated by one degree relative to underlying offense. Includes sexual orientation and gender identity — broader than many states. Civil penalties additionally available under LAD.

elements: Recruiting, luring, enticing, transporting, providing, obtaining, or harboring a person
By means of force, threat of force, fraud, or coercion
For the purpose of labor or services
enhancements: Victim under 18: maximum Life, no consent defense
Multiple victims: consecutive sentences
Drug use to control victim: additional CDS charges
notes: NJ Human Trafficking Act (N.J.S.A. 2C:13-8). Sex and labor trafficking both covered. Minor victims: no defense of consent. Safe harbor for victims under N.J.S.A. 2C:13-9. Asset forfeiture.

offense_class: 3rd Degree Crime; 2nd Degree if threat of force
elements: Believing that an official proceeding or investigation is pending or about to be instituted
Attempts to induce or otherwise cause a witness or informant to testify falsely
OR to withhold testimony, information, or evidence
OR flee jurisdiction to avoid testifying
enhancements: Use or threat of force: 2nd Degree — N.J.S.A. 2C:28-5(a)(3)
NERA may apply for 2nd Degree
Retaliation against witness: hindering apprehension charge concurrent
notes: NJ witness tampering escalates to 2nd Degree if force or threats are used. NERA applies to 2nd Degree (85% served). Separate from jury tampering under N.J.S.A. 2C:29-4.

statute_title: Tampering with a Juror or Jurors
elements: Attempting to influence a juror's vote, opinion, or action
In relation to a case or proceeding
Without official authority and otherwise than by lawful argument
enhancements: Bribery of juror: concurrent bribery charge — N.J.S.A. 2C:27-6
Force used: 2nd Degree concurrent
During capital case: aggravating factor
notes: NJ jury tampering is 3rd Degree. Bribery of juror is separately charged under N.J.S.A. 2C:27-6 (3rd Degree). Contact with potential jurors during voir dire also covered.

statute_title: Contempt of Court / Violation of Court Order
offense_class: 4th Degree Crime (FRO violation); contempt power for other violations
elements: Willful disobedience of a court order
Including protective orders, injunctions, or other court-ordered prohibitions
enhancements: FRO violation with assault: concurrent aggravated assault
Repeat contempt: enhanced by court
Civil contempt until compliance: coercive confinement possible
notes: FRO (Final Restraining Order) violation is 4th Degree Criminal Contempt. TRO violation handled as civil contempt. Separate statutory contempt power under Court Rules. Combined civil/criminal proceedings common.

offense_class: 4th Degree Crime (impersonation only); 3rd Degree (if deceiving or taking action)
elements: Pretending to be a public servant
With purpose to induce another to submit to pretended official authority
OR take or withhold action based on the impersonation
enhancements: Pretend arrest or search: 3rd Degree
Obtaining money through impersonation: fraud concurrent
Use of realistic badge, vehicle, or uniform: aggravating factor
notes: NJ impersonating public servant. Using impersonation to commit another offense elevates to 3rd Degree. Fake traffic stops and 'cop pulls' increasingly prosecuted. False credentials separate offense under N.J.S.A. 2C:21-17.

elements: Committing any crime or offense
For the benefit of, at the direction of, or in association with a criminal street gang
With knowledge that the group is a criminal street gang
mandatory_minimum: None; runs consecutive to underlying offense
enhancements: Underlying crime is 1st or 2nd Degree: gang enhancement is 2nd Degree
Prior gang conviction: extended term
Recruitment of juvenile: additional charge
notes: NJ street gang enhancement under N.J.S.A. 2C:33-29. Consecutive to underlying offense. Requires proving gang membership and gang-related motive. Gang recruitment of juveniles separately criminalized.

elements: Knowingly having in possession or under control
Any destructive device, explosive device, or bomb
Without lawful authority
mandatory_minimum: Graves Act may apply if used as weapon
enhancements: Use in or near school: mandatory additional term
Intent to terrorize: terroristic threats concurrent — N.J.S.A. 2C:12-3
Actual detonation: additional arson or assault charges
notes: NJ destructive devices under N.J.S.A. 2C:39-3. Prohibited weapons statute. Federal prosecution under 18 U.S.C. § 844 concurrent for explosives. Manufacturing explosives is additionally charged.

elements: Willfully making a false statement or misrepresentation
In connection with an application for public assistance (NJ FamilyCare, SNAP, TANF)
With intent to fraudulently obtain benefits
enhancements: SNAP/federal benefits: federal prosecution concurrent
Medicaid fraud: additional charges — N.J.S.A. 2C:51-5
Organized benefits fraud: multiple counts
notes: NJ public assistance fraud graded by amount obtained. Medicaid fraud (N.J.S.A. 2C:51-5) carries enhanced penalties. SNAP fraud also subject to federal prosecution. Restitution and benefit disqualification mandatory.
